expectations.text: The query handles ingestion delay explicitly: it uses ingestion_time() or declares a delay/wait window (e.g. let query_wait / ingestion_delay) that is added to the scan window
expectations.evidence: OVERRIDE of auto-grade (auto regex missed the CamelCase name). Query declares 'let IngestionDelayAllowance = 30m;   // Entra sign-in logs typically land 5-30 min late' (line 65) and applies it as '| where LastFailure > ago(RunFrequency + IngestionDelayAllowance)' (line 109), i.e. the delay is added to the per-run activity window; the event scan itself is the wider 4h window (line 84). Caveat: ingestion_time() is not used, so an IP whose spray is still active will re-fire on consecutive hourly runs (mitigated only by 12h incident grouping), and the guard is on TimeGenerated, so an event ingested >90 min late is scanned but never alerted. The handling is explicit and deliberate, so this passes on the assertion as written.

claims.claim: Every customDetails / alertDetailsOverride column survives the final projection
claims.evidence: All 13 customDetails values, the placeholders {{IPAddress}} {{DistinctFailedUsers}} {{HitUserCount}} {{FailedAttempts}} {{FailureRatio}} and alertSeverityColumnName Severity are listed in the final '| project' at lines 127-146; dynamic set columns are tostring()'d first (lines 120-126).

Two coupling hazards documented but not eliminated: 'let LookbackWindow = 4h; // MUST equal queryPeriod' and 'let RunFrequency = 1h; // MUST equal queryFrequency' (lines 63-64) duplicate the YAML schedule inside the query. Without ingestion_time() an active spray re-alerts every hour (acknowledged in the description; relies on incident grouping). Result code 530032 is real (user blocked due to risk) but unusual; 50158 omitted from the credential-valid list.

suggestions.assertion: The query handles ingestion delay explicitly: it uses ingestion_time() or declares a delay/wait window (e.g. let query_wait / ingestion_delay) that is added to the scan window
suggestions.reason: The assertion accepts a declared delay variable regardless of how it is used. A 'let ingestion_delay' that is only referenced in a post-aggregation recency guard (run A) and one that actually bounds the run slice via ingestion_time() (run B) both pass, yet only the latter prevents hourly re-alerting on the same events. Consider requiring that the run window itself is selected on ingestion_time().

suggestions.assertion: rule.yaml includes incident grouping or suppression settings (incidentConfiguration.groupingConfiguration or suppressionDuration) or alert enrichment (customDetails / alertDetailsOverride)
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfiable: any rule with a customDetails block passes even with no incident grouping or suppression. All three runs pass; the OR makes it non-discriminating. Split into 'incident grouping configured' and 'customDetails/alertDetailsOverride columns exist in the output'.

No assertion checks that customDetails / alertDetailsOverride placeholder columns actually survive the final projection (only the IP entity column is checked). This was correct in all three runs but is a common deploy-time failure and worth its own assertion.

No assertion checks for the time-window coupling trap: a hard-coded 'where TimeGenerated > ago(X)' inside the query that must equal queryPeriod (run A) silently diverges from the YAML when either is edited. 'Deploy without surprises' arguably covers this.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1, 6 and 7 are discriminating (they caught real gaps in other runs); 8 is trivially satisfied, and 2 passes a weaker design (delay used as a recency guard without ingestion_time()) that still re-alerts hourly.
